entries: `muse sessions --json` lists the sessions running on this machine, with who opened each one and whether it can be attached; `muse sessions --watch --json` keeps printing the list as sessions start and end

Several clients connected to the same session host can now drive one session together: each `session/resume` joins as a co-driver instead of refusing `sessionInUse`, submissions run one at a time in order (a busy submit queues unless it asks to steer or replace), and `driveHolder` names the earliest live driver
Send messages to running Muse sessions from the command line, including from the session itself

Session protocol serves `turn/modelAttemptStarted` each time a model attempt starts, before the provider is contacted, so apps can show the model as thinking only once it is working; in the TypeScript SDK, `ViewEvent` and `StaleDroppableMethod` gain `turn/modelAttemptStarted`, so code that matches them exhaustively needs a new case

`ItemKind` gains `subagentInput` — session-protocol clients get one item for each input a session sent to a subagent, when it was queued and when it was delivered, and a delivered subagent result names the row its Finished marker follows, so a client can show those rows in record order on resume
The agent now leaves a notice when it creates a goal or a cron job for you, and `/cron` lists and removes your scheduled jobs

The TypeScript and Python SDKs can now list a session's tasks, skills, and hooks, pause and resume workflows, request a recap, submit feedback, open a side chat, and search stored sessions without raw protocol calls
Session protocol reads of a forked session now report whether it came from a conversation rewind (`forkedFrom.isRewind`)

`muse attach --stdio <SESSION_ID> [-- <serve flags>]` connects a client's stdin and stdout to the host that holds a session, starting the session's own host with those serve flags when none does (except `--trust-workspace`, which a started host does not take), the same way locally and over ssh; it exits 4 when a TUI, `muse exec` or an older muse already holds the session

`muse serve --per-session` serves each connection from a fresh host of its own, which lists its sessions so another client can open and steer them with `muse attach --stdio <id>`; answers and notifications match plain `muse serve`, except that the host keeps running after your input ends (so no `session/closed` arrives) and its own diagnostics go to a log file instead of stderr; it does not take `--trust-workspace`

Settlement is refused only while a live driver holds the session: an attached observer's `turn/unqueue`, `approval/decide`, and `userInput/*` settlement refuse `sessionInUse` (naming how to join the drivers) while another live driver holds, and settle without taking drive once nobody drives, while observing prompts and replaying settled commands stay available
The TypeScript and Python SDK clients can send protocol commands the SDK does not wrap yet with `client.command`, which refuses the commands the SDK manages itself
`muse mcp list` and `muse mcp get` show configured MCP servers with their source, transport, and sign-in status

The TypeScript and Python SDKs can now run a turn in one call with `session.run`, which returns the final answer text, the turn's items, and its token usage, and stops the turn on an abort signal or task cancellation

`muse attach <session-ref>` opens this terminal attached to a session that is already running, as a second driver on the same timeline; unknown, ambiguous, not-running, and not-attachable references refuse with the reason and open no terminal

A client connected to `muse serve` over the session protocol can now list a session's subagents (running and finished) with ids, definition paths, parent, state, and result readiness, instead of parsing parent-stream child records
Sessions served by `muse serve` now remember the recovery mode a client picks when starting or resuming them, and reading a loaded session reports which mode is in effect and where it came from

Session protocol: a delivered subagent input item now carries `deliveredBeforeTurnEnd: true` when the subagent took that input before its parent's turn ended, so a client resuming the session can tell an interrupted turn from a finished one
`muse mcp add` and `muse mcp add-json` save MCP servers to user settings or the project file
`muse mcp remove` deletes MCP servers from user settings or the project file

When a command asks to run outside the sandbox, its approval prompt now offers "Always allow outside the sandbox in this workspace" for that command, so later runs of it there skip the prompt; an older Muse version can't resume a session that showed this choice until it updates
A session's peer-message history index is now a file inside the session folder, so a session folder copied to another machine resumes without rebuilding it
`muse serve` clients can run one model completion with no session, cancel it, and get its text, stop reason, model and token counts
A session protocol `subagent` item now names the subagent whose own session spawned it (`parentSubagentId`), so a client can file a nested subagent under its parent instead of under the root session
After a plan, the reply now says in plain words that nothing has changed yet and that you can reply `go` to start or say what to adjust
Clarified instructions for reading prior reports in Workflow children
Read long text lines in full when they fit the output limit, with byte-range guidance for larger lines

On `muse serve --listen`, only the client driving a session can change its approval mode or permission profile; other connected clients get `drive_required` and can take the drive with `session/resume` once the driving client disconnects
Workflows can read complete results from finished workers
The resume picker preview of a long, compacted chat shows its recent conversation, the same history you see after resuming

Compaction checkpoints keep answered questions and approval choices in a smaller form that holds no answer text; chats whose checkpoint holds one require a compatible app update, and older versions cannot open them
When Esc pauses a goal, the pause notice now stands out, the status bar and one reminder after your next message name `/goal resume`, and `/goal` lists the commands you can use
`/hud` can show the current session ID in the bottom status bar, the same ID `/status` reports
Paging back through a compacted chat over the session protocol now ends at one earlier-conversation item, as reading the chat does, and an older cursor before it answers that the view was truncated
`/feedback` uses the compressed upload that keeps sessions of up to about 760 MiB from the first launch, without waiting for Muse Code to fetch its remote settings

Incoming session messages now reach the client when the session protocol client is on: pending queue rows show the sender, effect label, and body, and delivered messages appear in the transcript, matching the classic client
In the `muse serve` session protocol, a finished workflow now lists its agents in the workflow's own order rather than the order they started, so every client numbers them the same way
Session protocol now streams the model's narration between tool calls as it is written, like final answers; saved chats do not change, so older versions still open them

The resume picker's comfortable view (`ctrl+o`) now explains why workspace status is unavailable — whether the workspace is not trusted, the probe sandbox is unavailable, or the status check failed — instead of silently omitting it; the default dense view is unchanged

Session protocol now marks a streaming message as narration or as the answer from its first word, so clients can show narration as narration while it is written; clients that ignore the mark see no change
The TypeScript and Python SDKs find `muse` on `PATH` when you do not pass a host path to `spawn`, and say what they searched when no host is found
Confirming a conversation rewind now shows "Preparing rewind…" right away, and the action rows stop showing a selection, so it is clear the rewind is underway before the server answers

When a waiting background notice keeps being refused its wake-up, the saved session now notes which hold refused it, so a stalled helper can be traced; an older Muse build cannot open a session holding this note, so update the app to open it (other sessions are unaffected)

Muse Code no longer updates a shared task (its status, plan, or fields) just because the task's own text or agent hints tell agents to; it does the work you asked for, then offers the update and waits for your yes

When you ask Muse Code to empty a directory or clean up files, its final answer now names what it removed and flags anything that looked unrelated to the task, such as another repository or a symlink into one

The TypeScript and Python SDK quickstart and cookbook recipes now teach the high-level client (`MuseClient.spawn`, `startSession`, `session.run`, `turn.cancel()`, `setModel`, `listModels`) instead of raw session protocol calls

A resumed chat whose saved view is damaged heals it from the log; a forked chat, which is not rebuilt, reports `projectionRebuildFailed` right away; health frames coalesce so the client sees the final state once
A loaded chat whose live view fails closed is re-loaded once from its log (weak registry hold, no reopen); a failed re-load announces `projectionRebuildFailed` once
After a `healthy` view-health signal, the client re-reads the view and adopts the turn state, skipping rows it already rendered
When the agent reads an image file, it now also sees the image's width and height in pixels, plus the original size when the image was scaled down, so positions it gives in pixels match the image

When you ask Muse Code to empty a directory or clean up files, it now lists what is there first, deletes what belongs to the task, and asks before deleting anything that looks unrelated, such as another repository, a symlink into one, or data; without your answer it keeps those items and says so

Bug fixes now get a focused failing test for each reported defect, and the regression test also covers the inputs the fix claims to handle beyond the reported one (another position or order, extreme or boundary values, and input rules the request restates), still without new test frameworks or extra full-suite runs

When you tell Muse Code about something the repository cannot show, such as a migration or a deployment that already happened, it now works from what you said, updates repository defaults that still point at the old setup, and remembers it in later turns instead of asking you to repeat it
Session discovery now lists up to 128 local and Claude sessions, up from 64; each machine still makes at most 64 of its live sessions discoverable until a later release raises that limit
Automatic Windows sandbox setup at startup now first explains the two local Windows accounts it creates or updates and what each one runs, then asks Yes or No; No exits without changing anything
When the only thing left is a background job the agent started, the turn now ends instead of the agent polling it; the job's completion or stuck-job notice wakes the agent to finish

When an answer compares many items on short numbers, such as estimates for several funds under several scenarios, Muse can now show them in one wider table that still fits a normal terminal instead of splitting them into narrow tables

The terminal UI now switches between light and dark themes when your terminal does, while a session is running, in terminals that report it (such as Ghostty, kitty and Contour), unless you set a fixed light or dark terminal background in `/theme`
Saved chats can now record that an approval is still being applied, so it settles exactly once after a restart; earlier versions can't open a chat that holds this record, and updating fixes it

When you ask whether something already built behaves correctly, the agent now checks each observation against the source the project follows, fixes only what is wrong, and keeps behavior that is correct, explaining why instead of removing it

When you ask for a 3D web page and the machine has no browser, Muse now installs a headless browser with the system package manager to check the page itself, and says plainly that the page was not run only if that install fails
When the agent reads a file with Windows (CRLF) line endings, it is told so, which makes it less likely to switch the line endings when it rewrites the file
On Windows, the agent is guided to write PowerShell commands such as `Select-String` and `$env:NAME = ...` instead of Unix commands such as `grep` and `export`, which PowerShell does not have
Muse Code keeps closely linked facts in one sentence, so fix and build summaries read as connected sentences instead of one fact per line
While a goal waits on something outside the session that ends at a known time, such as a soak or a cooldown, the agent schedules a one-time wake-up for just after that time instead of only snoozing

Saved chats can now record that the 3D generation service accepted a job, so its job ID is not lost if the call is stopped; earlier versions can't open a chat that holds this record, and updating fixes it

Resuming a session over the session protocol with a `modelId` now records that model the way `muse resume --model` does, and a model the host refuses keeps the session on its saved model instead of failing the resume
MCP servers and hooks now get your proxy settings (`HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY`), as other apps do
When more skills are installed than the skills catalog can list, built-in and prompt-named skills keep their full descriptions first and more of the other skills are left out to make room

A Muse build older than this release cannot open a chat in which a newer build resumed the session automatically after a crash and told the agent what was interrupted. Updating the app fixes it; other chats are unaffected

When you ask for a 3D web page in a sentence or two, Muse now checks it in one light pass (a desktop run, one input test, a fix and a final run) instead of its full review rounds, so short requests finish sooner; detailed briefs still get every check
Usage telemetry now trusts the certificate authority file set in `telemetry.ca_bundle`, so it keeps working on networks that re-sign TLS traffic with a company root certificate

Session-protocol clients: view cursors are now minted in the `v9:` spelling; a cursor in an older spelling is refused once with the standard "reopen without a cursor" guidance, and a view cache saved by an older build is rebuilt on first use, so no client silently skips or misreads events

When `muse serve` refuses a request to interrupt, stop, resume, reopen or close a subagent, the refusal now names the exact reason (for example `owner_not_running` or `attempt_history_unavailable`) instead of one general reason

A resumed session's snapshot now carries each Monitor's recent output lines, including the ones already delivered to the model, so a client shows the Monitor's tail right after resuming instead of an empty one

Muse follows your requests more closely: it answers a direct question first, keeps working when you send a question or remark mid-task, does not stop while a change you asked for is still unmade, asks its remaining questions before building on a partial answer, removes extras instead of hiding them when you ask it to simplify, asks you at once when a login only you can renew blocks the task, and no longer works around a download the environment blocks or a package index that fails its certificate check
Muse Spark 1.3 at `max` reasoning effort now gets the same full base instructions as every other model and effort, including the newer answer-style and grounding guidance

Through `muse serve` and the SDKs, stopping a subagent that has already stopped now answers `subagent_already_stopped` instead of `subagent_state_ineligible`, so a client can tell that race from a failed stop

Over the session protocol, a refusal caused by a session log deleted or replaced outside Muse now carries the error reason `session_log_lost` when resuming, sending or steering a message, compacting, renaming, forking, opening a side chat, leaving, controlling a subagent or workflow, or choosing an approval that saves something for later, so a client can recognize it without matching the message

Security: In `muse serve`, subagents and workflow agents now use the same approval mode as the session that started them, so an allow-all session no longer prompts for its subagents and a deny-unmatched session's workflow agents deny instead of asking

Security: Sessions in workspaces the user has not trusted no longer start any MCP servers. Startup withholds every configured server, shows one notice naming the withheld count and reason (project-scope servers are withheld unread, without being listed), and `/mcp` marks each knowable withheld server as "withheld: workspace untrusted". Trusting the workspace starts them on the next session
Security: Sandboxed Linux commands can no longer redirect their own approved network connections to a different local service than the one you approved
Security: A `!` shell command run in a session that `muse serve` hosts can no longer write the folders where Muse keeps its client credentials and settings
Security: In an untrusted workspace, the agent now asks for approval before writing to memory, showing what it wants to save, instead of running silently
Security: Sandboxed Linux commands can no longer redirect another concurrent command's approved network connections to a different local service than the one you approved
Security: A Meta API key after `Bearer` or `Authorization: token`, such as in a printed `curl -H` command or a provider error, is now hidden whole from the model, session logs and error output

Security: When a command running in the sandbox asks to reach a new host, Muse now asks for your approval before looking the hostname up, so a declined host is not looked up; only `localhost` names are still looked up first, to confirm they point at this computer, and a hostname that does not exist now also asks for approval before it fails

Security: A tool call's `shell` argument can now select only bash, zsh or sh (PowerShell or pwsh on Windows); any other value runs the default shell, so an approved command always runs under a shell you expect

Security: On Linux, sandboxed commands and file tools can no longer read sign-in details or settings in `~/.config/muse` and the other settings folders through a second mount of the same filesystem, such as WSL's `/mnt/wslg/distro` or a home folder bind-mounted at a second path; on such a computer a subagent started before updating can lose its work tools when it continues after `/resume`, and a command that walks that second mount reports the settings folders inside it as unreadable

Security: Muse no longer trusts its local session registry folder, or the startup folder of a session's own host, when it sits inside a folder another local user owns; that user could swap in folders of their own, and on a shared Mac change what is inside through folder settings
Security: A session's own host no longer starts through a folder link that another local user owns, even one reached through another link, since they could swap the link and move the host's files

Security: When your data folder's path is too long for its own socket, `muse attach --stdio` and `muse serve --per-session` now start their host under `/tmp/tbh-<uid>-rt` only when that folder is yours, mode 0700, and not a link (they create it when it is missing); otherwise they stop with an error that says how to fix it

Security: `/feedback` now removes more kinds of secrets, such as passwords in connection strings, authorization headers, JWTs and common API key formats, from your note, the recent activity, crash reports, the screen snapshot and the configuration snapshot before upload. Text that follows a secret-looking label, such as `token:` or `password:`, is hidden too, so a note titled "Auth token: refresh loop" is filed as "Auth token: [REDACTED]"

Security: A host that `muse attach --stdio` or `muse serve --per-session` starts now refuses a startup file that something changed after it was written, so another session cannot alter what the host starts with
When a subagent's result arrives on its own while the parent agent is doing other work, the parent is now told where to read the subagent's whole answer instead of only its first 512 characters
A recovered subagent's child view now shows its retained result after an explicit result read instead of an empty result slot
Model list no longer shows saved models the server does not serve

A chat whose compaction keeps failing to save its checkpoint no longer pays for a new summary on every request; after 2 failures in a row Muse stops automatic compaction for that chat, shows one error naming the cause, and tries again when you reopen the chat or a compaction works
A session parked waiting on watched external work now resumes when a watcher change event or a background task completion arrives, instead of staying on Working until interrupted
Moving another file onto `session-index.db` while Muse Code runs no longer shows the replaced file's sessions (unless another program has the new file open at that moment) or crashes the app
In the classic Windows console, such as a plain PowerShell window, the prompt and status symbols now show as readable characters instead of boxes with question marks
A turn keeps working after a long-running command it was polling completes
Retrying a queued turn that restart recovery abandoned now reports it as abandoned instead of looking still queued
Background work status results now tell the agent that completion arrives automatically, so it stops repeatedly checking status while a long command runs and waits for the delivered result instead
Late background updates keep stopped Monitors labeled as stopped
A fork reopened after it compacted no longer re-reads its whole history each turn, so damage in older history no longer stops it

A `muse serve` chat whose saved view fell behind its latest compaction now rebuilds that view from the compaction point when it is next opened, instead of re-reading the whole session log; earlier history shows collapsed behind the "earlier conversation restored from checkpoint" divider. If the records after the compaction point are damaged, the chat still opens and keeps working, starting from its newest message instead of refusing to resume

Opening a chat whose saved permission change was lost now shows the reset permission level when a resume would commit a reset, instead of the older, wider level. When the reset is refused or cannot be decided, it keeps showing the surviving level
Resuming a forked session no longer sometimes fails with a log-replay error that forced a recovery session instead
A monitor that stops itself for noise, timeout, or a closed stream now always records its stop reason in the session
When `/feedback` has to shorten a long session record twice to fit the upload, the notice after sending now shows the kept and dropped sizes of the record that was actually sent
Resumed forked sessions keep the grouped Ran commands card instead of expanded raw output
Moving a larger session index onto `session-index.db` while Muse Code runs no longer leaves the session list failing as a corrupt index

A chat whose newest compaction checkpoint belongs to a cancelled turn now refuses to resume, read, or fork with a clear error instead of reloading history from before the checkpoint; use `muse export` to recover its log

A compaction no longer leaves its checkpoint unwritten when the saved chat view is momentarily behind; the checkpoint is saved and the view catches up or is rebuilt from it the next time the chat is opened

A reminder whose duty names a tool that does not exist, or has a malformed tool token, is now turned off when the session starts, with a notice in the TUI and in `tbh exec` output that names the reminder and the token and says how to fix it, instead of failing silently each time it would run (under `tbh serve` it is turned off without a notice for now)
Two Muse Code processes that recreate a deleted session index at the same moment no longer lose one side's first writes
A session parked waiting on a Monitor watcher now resumes on that watcher's change lines even when the watcher was started by the canonical Monitor path, instead of staying parked until interrupted
Reopening a compacted conversation no longer runs completed queued messages again
A session that paused to wait now resumes when its background task finishes instead of staying stuck until you intervene
Running /compact in a long session with a saved context checkpoint no longer freezes the terminal for tens of seconds and then fails with "no compactable run is available"
Replies that switch into another script (such as Chinese characters) mid-task are now retried once so progress text stays in your language
A fork or side chat of a fork that has compacted starts from that fork's newest checkpoint instead of re-reading its whole history
Parallel tool calls start their hooks without waiting for each other
A resumed command with an unrecognized result status no longer shows as succeeded
Agent acts on a finished background task instead of waiting for the next message
Cancelling or steering a run waiting on a covered external wait now takes the cancel or supersede exit instead of reporting an error or resuming
`session/read` on a subagent's session no longer keeps showing its worktree as `active`, or a delivered input as queued, when the parent recorded the change during an earlier read
A tool call that finished just before a crash no longer keeps its settled row after resume; the resumed view marks it `— unresolved` so an uncertain outcome is never shown as settled

Subagent guidance now tells the parent agent to fetch a truncated child answer itself instead of spawning a reader, to poll long waits without a fresh watcher subagent per round, and to stay silent instead of posting a status update every time a subagent returns with nothing new to report

Typing into a prompt you recalled with Up no longer throws away the message you were writing; the recalled prompt shows `· edited` next to its history position, and Down or Esc brings your unsent message back
Over the session protocol, a reread or resumed compacted chat no longer keeps showing restored earlier messages from a turn that was taken back

File edits in Windows-style (CRLF) files now match multi-line text written with plain line breaks and keep the file's CRLF line endings in the replacement; a failed edit says when only the line endings differ
A forked chat that opened in the terminal but failed to load elsewhere now opens in all clients
Background work waits no longer loop on repeated status checks that burn turns

Answers and other tool results that mention bearer tokens in plain words, such as "JWT bearer tokens", now reach the model unchanged instead of showing a redaction marker the model could copy into code; real bearer credentials are still hidden
A resume whose load quarantines a corrupt cron database now reports it on `session/resume`, so the client shows the warning row once
A parked run resumes when the watcher task it waits on finishes
When the same plain model failure stops two turns back to back with nothing shown between them, it now appears once while the session runs, as it already does after a resume
Built-in skills you start with a slash command now name tools the way the model is offered them, so it calls them by the right name (not yet with `--no-session-log`)
Built-in skills that a custom agent preloads now name tools the way that agent's model is offered them, so it calls them by the right name
The SDKs no longer list a question from a turn that already finished as still waiting for an answer after a resume
Default Light theme: darker secondary, success, warning, accent and stroke colors for readable contrast on white
Forking a session, or opening a side chat from it, no longer fails with "invalid_target" when the session compacted and later saved a checkpoint while catching up
Research workflows use complete large results through verification and report synthesis
Sessions started on standalone `muse serve` with a plain `session/start` now get an automatic name, served on `session/read` at start and after the first turn, like the TUI's embedded host

A Workflow whose script already finished no longer fails because one read of its records failed briefly while its final summary was being built; it retries for a short while, and a read that keeps failing fails the Workflow with a reason saying its records could not be read
A finished background task no longer starts a second agent turn beside one that is still working, which refused compaction checkpoints
The quota pace offer ("You're using your quota fast") now appears in sessions on the new TUI client just as in classic sessions, instead of never showing
A chat no longer compacts early just because a background detail such as its session name was filled in after the first reply; the context-size estimate now counts only what actually changed
Background-task results and monitor events queued while the chat sits idle are delivered without waiting for your next keypress; a parked end-of-turn wait no longer strands them for hours

A session whose saved history no longer matched its live record of a turn now keeps saving compaction checkpoints instead of failing every attempt until a restart, so it still resumes from its latest compaction

An image wider or taller than 2048 pixels, up to 6144, sent over the session protocol, such as a full-screen screenshot, is now resized to fit 2048 pixels before the model sees it, as in the terminal app, so apps can show its thumbnail in the sent prompt and rewind and resume keep the image
A rotated phone photo that is resized or re-encoded before the model sees it, because it is over 2048 pixels or 2 MiB, now stays upright instead of turning sideways
On a store kept on an NFSv3 mount, a chat's history in `muse serve` stays readable after a restart instead of being reported unavailable
Workflow reports retain earlier results after a subagent follow-up
Running `/compact` keeps its progress indicator visible while the summary is being prepared

Resuming a compacted session whose last turn was taken back now shows the conversation since the last compaction, as the other clients do, instead of replaying the whole log or showing the taken-back turn's summary
When a finished background task wakes the agent, the waiting turn now ends first, so it cannot resume beside the new turn and block its checkpoints

After a crash and resume, orphaned background monitor calls now revise to "Review … unresolved" like other orphaned tools instead of keeping their pre-crash settled text, and the revised row keeps its duration stamp

Long sessions that run Workflows nonstop keep saving their resume checkpoints. A checkpoint no longer keeps every finished child of a Workflow that has ended, which grew it until saving failed after about 2,000 children. Asking a child of a long-finished Workflow for more work now explains that the Workflow has ended. Opening a session compacted this way needs this app version or later

`/goal resume` now starts the resumed turn when it is sent while a turn or a `!shell` is running, or at the moment the goal reminder pauses the goal; before, the goal could show as active while nothing ran
Long tasks no longer stop early after announcing the next step; shell commands that already finished no longer block the agent from continuing

`view/subscribe` from earlier history of a session whose latest compaction belonged to a turn that was taken back now refuses with the same error as reading the session, instead of pointing the client at a cursor that gives the same answer again
After you store a different API key or sign in to another account, a restarted `muse serve` lists that credential's models instead of the previous credential's saved model list
Side chats opened by session-protocol clients keep the workspace, model and MCP tools of the session they branch from
Apps connected to Muse Code no longer show a hook that blocked a prompt as a rejection when that block never took effect
After starting a long command in the background, the agent ends its turn and reports the result when it finishes, instead of sometimes waiting up to five minutes and missing the finish
Resuming an older session from a connected client no longer drops an earlier completed turn from the model's context, or names it as unreadable, when a leftover restart followed it
When the model catalog service answers with no models, the app now reports the catalog fetch as failed instead of silently emptying the model list
`/rewind` no longer offers points from before a compacted summary in older sessions whose summary cannot start a branch; the points after it are shown as unavailable instead
On macOS and Linux, a damaged saved-session index is now set aside and rebuilt automatically, so `/resume` no longer stays slow until the file is removed by hand
The terminal now redraws the chat area when its window regains focus, so a garbled frame recovers instead of staying broken
A forked session keeps its folder, model and provider in the session list after its first turn, instead of being listed with none
Commentary and tool text that flips into French, Spanish, or Indonesian during an English session is now resampled like foreign-script flips
Reading a very large session through `muse serve` now returns its details with pageable history instead of failing with "response exceeds the outbound frame limit"
Preserve session recovery state when saving the next checkpoint

Resuming or forking a session whose last turn was taken back after it saved a checkpoint without compacting now continues from the previous compaction, instead of refusing the session or replaying the whole log
Standalone `muse serve` generates session titles when automatic naming is on

Reopening a session no longer makes the agent start a turn by itself to react to a background command that quitting had stopped. The reopened transcript then shows the command as backgrounded, with no finished row

Paging back through a session that was compacted under an older version now stops at the earlier-conversation summary once the session has been read, as reading it does, instead of showing the history from before the compaction; after a new turn, that history can still appear until the session is read again

A file link whose label is its own absolute path now shows that absolute path in the TUI transcript instead of shortening it to a workspace-relative path, so asking for a file's full path gets the full path
A session no longer becomes unreadable ("MalformedJsonl") after it compacts its context while a turn and a background task's follow-up are running at the same time
Resuming a chat from a saved position after `view/unsubscribe` no longer sends an event twice when a change lands while the resume is reading history
A session started with `/goal` is no longer named after Muse's hidden goal instructions in `/resume` and in apps that list your sessions; it shows your first prompt, or no title until you send one

After resuming a long session, a new agent can no longer reuse the name of a child from a long-finished Workflow under the same parent. Before, the resumed session allowed the name while the full session history refused it. Opening a session that holds such a name needs this app version or later

A session waiting at the end of a turn now wakes when a result arrives that would wake an idle session, such as a failed background command or a message another session sent to wake it, including one that arrived just before it began waiting for background work, instead of staying on Working until you type

A session reopened after the previous process stopped in the middle of a batch of tool calls now keeps saving compaction checkpoints instead of failing every attempt, so it still resumes from its latest compaction
Built-in skills you start with a slash command in the terminal app now name tools the way the model is offered them in every session, including ones started with `--no-session-log`
A checkpoint records its foreign-prefix length, so resume of a log with foreign lines below the checkpoint no longer refuses on the ordinal check
Stopping a subagent after another message now ends its running work instead of only marking it cancelled
An active `/goal` keeps working on its own after a reply that did not continue it, instead of waiting for you to send another message
Resuming a session saved by an older version whose last turn was taken back after it wrote a checkpoint without compacting now continues from the previous compaction instead of refusing the session

In `muse serve`, a resumed or forked chat whose saved reasoning effort is `ultra` now runs at `xhigh` while `ultra` is unavailable, as a newly chosen `ultra` already does; the saved choice is kept and applies again once `ultra` is available, unless you set the effort again in the meantime
When Muse dies on a memory fault (for example a disk that fills up mid-session), your terminal is put back to normal instead of being left without echo until you run `reset`
After a chat reopens from a crash, queued follow-ups and background results now wait for your next message instead of starting a reply on their own

Resumed sessions keep the Workflow tool again, including sessions saved by an older version; when a session's saved Workflow version can't be used, it uses the version a new session gets instead of asking you to start a new session
A browser game built on a remote machine now hands off an SSH tunnel command with its local URL, so you can open it from your own computer
Several `muse serve` processes sharing one data folder no longer grow the session index write-ahead log by about one index size every few seconds, which could fill the disk
In long turns, skill, memory and to-do suggestions now still see your latest request, so a suggestion no longer contradicts it, such as adding tests when you only asked for an explanation
A session an app or SDK starts with a chosen model keeps that model in session lists and after the host restarts, instead of switching to the host's default model
Settings, credential, and trust files larger than 16 MiB are now refused with an error instead of being read into memory whole
When one agent in a Workflow cannot confirm that its start was saved (for example, because the disk is full), the Workflow's other agents now keep running instead of being stopped

`/goal resume` in the terminal now puts the goal back to paused when the resumed turn then fails to start for good, so another `/goal resume` can start it; before, the goal could show as active while nothing ran
When a finished background task wakes the agent after a resumed goal turn, its result now waits for the next turn instead of running beside it, which refused compaction checkpoints
A session waiting at the end of a turn no longer stops waiting early because of a message from another session that it already read during that turn
Keep Monitor stop status tied to its source session after a rewind

Paging back through a compacted `muse serve` chat now stops at the earlier-conversation summary from the first page when its view was rebuilt, and for a chat compacted under an older version it keeps stopping there after a new turn once the session has been read
File paths with apostrophes display correctly in `/rules`
When you tell the agent to stay inside one folder, it keeps its throwaway test scripts there instead of writing them under `/tmp`
A session you fork or start through `muse attach --stdio` beside the one it opened is now listed by `muse sessions` and reopens on the same host with `muse attach --stdio <id>` while that host runs
A background compaction summary that finishes while an internal turn is already running now installs after that turn ends, instead of mid-turn where its checkpoint was refused
Pending message batches keep sent messages marked as sent when delivery remains unconfirmed
`session-message send` reports success after a Linux session accepts the message
Sending a session message no longer stalls while another session updates the session list
On Linux, messages sent from inside a session now show as accepted instead of unverified

Several `muse serve` processes sharing one data folder no longer rewrite the session-name list in the session index on every maintenance pass, so session list subscribers stop getting a change notification every few seconds

Sending or resuming a session no longer fails with "projection failed: tool-result clear entry did not match" when a stored clear record matches no result or matches more than one; the bad entry is skipped and the session continues with the old output left in context
The `/resume` preview of a session a `/goal` drove no longer shows Muse's hidden goal prompts as your messages
Resuming a session with a side chat no longer fails
Worktree sessions load project skills, rules and hooks from the worktree copy, so edits there take effect and skill files stay readable
Opening an older, never-compacted session from a connected client for the first time no longer reports a stale `runtime_turn_task_lost` failure from a leftover restart as its last turn
`muse serve` now frees a session's memory when the session is left or unloaded, so a long-running server no longer grows with every session it has served
Scheduled and background wakes queued while the agent is idle no longer wait for your next message after a lost wake-up signal — the runtime re-queues the wake itself once the blocking state clears

A `muse serve` chat that was compacted and has an unusable saved view (unreadable, or left as a terminal marker) now builds that view from its latest compaction point when it is next opened, instead of re-reading the whole session log; earlier history shows collapsed behind the "earlier conversation restored from checkpoint" divider, and records missing or damaged before the compaction point no longer stop the chat from opening
Resuming after successful context compaction no longer shows a false interruption warning
Show MCP tool and server names while a call is running
Resuming a chat with a lost record above a checkpoint reopens with permissions reset to defaults and a warning instead of refusing
When you dismiss or interrupt a question prompt, the agent now treats the unanswered questions as still open and asks about them again before building on them

Recovering (`muse workflows recover --apply`) or resuming a workflow interrupted on Muse Code 1.4.5 or earlier keeps its finished agent calls, reruns the ones that were still running from the start, and says which model each rerun used
Agent cards show the total number of tool calls
Answering a pending question right after a crash resume works again: a submit that meets a full queue waits for the next drain instead of dropping
A resumed subagent's turn now waits until a background task wake or a compaction install in its session finishes, instead of running beside it where compaction checkpoints were refused

`muse serve` no longer sends `"cost": null` in a session snapshot's token usage before the first model reply, which made schema-checking clients reject the snapshot; an unpriced cost is now left out, as the protocol schema defines
Fixed subagents failing when receiving a message after the parent conversation was compacted
The TUI no longer occasionally runs one needless extra auto-compaction right after a compaction that happened during a reply, in a reopened session, or after a background task's reply

On a Mac, when you ask for a link to a page Muse built, Muse now gives the file path or the start command right away instead of asking what to do, and says plainly when a server it started stops as Muse quits

`session/resume` of a side chat now reports the chat it came from in `sideFrom`, as `session/sideChat` already does, and no longer reports it in `forkedFrom`; `session/list` now reports `sideFrom: null` for a just-opened side chat too, as it already does for every other session
Subagent retries return the saved creation result when execution recovery is unavailable
Fixed a task-history error that could prevent interrupted Workflows from resuming after a restart

When the verify observer reviews a finished turn, it can now see the end of a long tool result, where a check usually prints whether it passed, as well as the result's start — so a task that already passed its check is less likely to be sent to verify again
Paging back through a `muse serve` chat compacted under an older version now stops at the earlier-conversation summary from the first page after a resume, even when a new turn lands before that page
A session resumed thousands of times, for example by repeated `exec` runs, no longer saves every resume's start records in each checkpoint, which had made its checkpoints too large to save
Resumed workflow reports retain results completed before the pause
When Muse fails to start because of a setting, the error a session shows now also says to fix the setting and start Muse again
Prevent interrupted subagents from failing or repeatedly waking when background commands finish
Keep compaction progress visible in reopened sessions
`muse mcp get` and `muse mcp list` text failures now print the pending MCP warnings ahead of the error line, matching the `--json` stderr behavior
In `muse serve`, a text message that starts or steers a turn on a stuck session that cannot take more commands now fails after 30 seconds with a busy error you can retry, instead of never answering
In the TypeScript and Python SDKs, `turn.unqueue()` now always hands back the queued draft it reclaimed, whatever order the server's replies arrive in

A long session no longer saves every past prompt's intake records in each checkpoint, only those whose message the saved conversation still holds, so checkpoints of sessions with thousands of turns stay small enough to save
`muse mcp list` and `muse mcp get` fault reports now name the exact project file at fault and classify non-file settings paths correctly
`muse mcp list` and `muse mcp get` report an error when repository markers cannot be read instead of silently omitting project servers

In a short terminal, the rewind confirmation keeps its warnings and the selected action on screen, Enter no longer confirms an action the screen could not show, and a terminal too short for any action asks you to make it taller

When a running session's log file or folder is deleted or replaced outside Muse while Muse is saving to it, Muse no longer starts a new log partway through or writes into the replacement. It says the log was deleted or replaced, stops saving that session and refuses new messages and setting changes there; run Muse again to start a new session. A lost log of another conversation, such as a side chat's, stops saving only that conversation. If the log file itself was moved away instead, Muse says so and saving resumes once you move it back

After the session log is deleted or replaced outside Muse, answering an approval with allow once, allow for this session or reject still reaches the waiting tool and the turn finishes; once Muse has noticed the loss, a choice that would save a rule for later is refused and says why

After a session log is deleted or replaced outside Muse, renaming the session, changing permissions or a setting, sending a message, `/compact`, `/new`, `/clear`, rewinding, and messaging, following up with, resuming or reopening a subagent from its view say so and what to do instead of a generic or misleading error, from the first thing you do after the deletion; a `/goal` change the running turn already received is no longer shown as still waiting to reach the model; leaving the session over the session protocol says so when its log was replaced; and `muse exec` no longer adds a second error at exit or says it flushed the logs when a signal stops it

When a session log is moved or deleted outside Muse, turn and leave errors over the session protocol and the `muse serve` stop line say so and how to get saving back, `/export trajectory` says the log is missing and to move it back instead of suggesting `--no-session-log`, and `/new` or `/clear` held back by another conversation's moved log names it

After a session log is deleted or replaced outside Muse, `/fork` and `/side` say so and start nothing, even when one is the first thing you do after the deletion; `/resume` into another conversation, such as a side chat, whose log was lost while Muse was saving it alongside this one is refused before it can stop the current conversation's running turn or background work; and when you leave a session whose log was lost, its notice says so and no longer offers to resume it, whether that session did not shut down cleanly or Muse stopped waiting for it to shut down, and the "To continue this session" line that `/clear` and `/new` show for it is removed when that notice appears

When a session log is replaced outside Muse, or deleted on macOS or Linux, while a save to it is still unconfirmed, Muse now says the log was lost instead of reporting a failed flush every time, and another conversation's lost log, such as a side chat's, no longer holds back new messages, `/fork`, `/side` or new subagents in the conversation you are in

While a confirmed conversation rewind is preparing, the exit key (Ctrl-D, or your remapped exit binding) works again: the first press shows the "press again to quit" hint on the rewind screen, and when work is still running the exit confirmation appears and Stay or Esc returns to the rewind

When you ask for a plan in a file, the agent now saves it at the path you named (or a visible spot in your project) and replies with the link, a one-line verdict, and the key decisions instead of pasting the whole plan into chat
On a Mac, after Muse hands you a file path or a start command for a page, Muse no longer goes back to start a hidden background server for it
A host started by `muse attach --stdio` or `muse serve --per-session` no longer stops taking connections or ignores `SIGTERM` for as long as one of its sessions is slow to respond
A model whose catalogue entry gives its context window but no output limit now shows in the model list, keeps that window for compaction, and uses the standard output limit

Paging back through a `muse serve` chat compacted under an older version now stops at the earlier-conversation summary even when the session was never resumed or read since the server started, instead of showing the history from before the compaction

On a short terminal during a running turn, the plan panel now folds to fewer rows instead of pushing the live status row (token use, when the HUD tokens field is on) out of view, so the current plan and token use stay visible together
Prevent empty background notifications from adding turns or blocking rewind

Terminals that show program status (OSC 7501) now see Muse as working while a turn started by a finished background task, a schedule, or another wake runs, instead of keeping the previous turn's done or idle state

In `muse serve`, a message that runs a skill on a stuck session, or a cancel sent to a stuck session that cannot take more commands, now fails after 30 seconds with a busy error you can retry, instead of an internal error (skill) or no answer (cancel)
A session reopened after the previous run was stopped while still saving now keeps saving compaction checkpoints instead of failing every one until the next restart
After a resume, answering a pending structured prompt no longer silently drops your Enter when a stray key lands before the retry sends; the staged answer still sends exactly once
Keep the compaction status visible after resuming a session

Paging back through a `muse serve` chat saved by an older version now also stops at the earlier-conversation summary when that chat was condensed by a periodic history checkpoint, or by a compaction whose checkpoint was skipped, instead of showing the history from before the checkpoint
Messages from hooks no longer appear as rows in the transcript; they show only as a brief status notice
A resumed session whose scheduled job fires as its first turn starts now saves that turn's compaction checkpoints instead of skipping them

When the agent checks on a command that is still running and the new output is longer than it asked to see, it now gets the newest output as well as the start, with a line counting the bytes left out between them, instead of only the oldest part
On a Mac, when you ask Muse to keep a server running, Muse now says it cannot keep it running after it quits and gives the command to start it, instead of promising to look after it

With many sessions running in their own processes, new TUI sessions and `muse exec` runs keep local session messaging: once only 16 of the 64 local session slots are free, sessions a program opens through `muse serve --per-session` (or as a further session over one `muse attach --stdio` connection) stop being listed in `muse sessions` instead of taking those slots, while each Desktop tab's own session, and the forks and side chats made on it, still register until all 64 are taken
A background task or workflow that finishes during a turn that compacts its context no longer makes every later turn fail with "event id … conflicts with an existing event"
Terminals that show program status (OSC 7501) now see Muse as working while it compacts context, starts a turn, or generates a recap you asked for, instead of the previous turn's done or idle state
Scheduled prompts with an hourly or faster cadence now fire during both passes of the repeated hour when daylight saving time ends, instead of skipping the second pass
Keep the compaction status visible after returning from a side chat
A session saved by one Muse Code build can take new prompts when a differently compiled build reopens it, instead of failing to send with an internal error

While a long command runs in the background, Muse no longer keeps re-checking its log file or process from new shell calls; it ends the turn for the automatic result or watches progress with the `Monitor` tool
Checkpoint-carried fork seeds the loader must accept are no longer refused as mismatched: covered turns and carrier children count the way the replay mints them

A host started by `muse attach --stdio` or `muse serve --per-session` whose last client left after a session stop timed out now exits once that stop finishes, instead of staying up until the session is unloaded for being idle
Assistant replies stay visible in short terminal windows
The Python SDK now derives its schema fingerprint from its wheel's bundled schema when imported from inside a source checkout, instead of the checkout's live schema
A session whose reminder list was lost across a restart now reopens instead of refusing every turn
Resumed subagents report a missing answer instead of empty success after exhausting their reminders
When the server refuses a login because the Muse Code app is deactivated, the login panel now shows that reason and that signing in again will not fix it, instead of saying the API key is invalid
Subagents are reminded to submit required results before reaching their step limit
A subagent's view keeps its activity in order across parent turns, and a cancelled or failed attempt's result row no longer reads Result ready

A long session no longer saves the approval history of every past tool call in each checkpoint, only approvals still pending, approvals that grant a session-wide permission, and those whose tool call the saved conversation still holds, so checkpoints of approval-heavy sessions stay small enough to save
A session whose workspace folder was deleted mid-session now recovers on the next tool call instead of failing every tool
Resuming a compacted session restores subagents that finished before the checkpoint instead of dropping their rows

Compaction now works up to the model's real context window instead of stopping at 512,000 tokens, and when Muse cannot tell which recent messages a turn must keep and so skips compaction, a turn larger than the context window now fails right away with a clear "could not fit within the model's context window" error instead of being sent for the provider to refuse

When a chat's own messages already fill the space compaction must keep, Muse no longer pays for a summary it would throw away on every request, and the compaction error names the kept messages as the cause
Resumed sessions can continue after an unrecorded tool result, with the outcome shown as unknown
Workflow retries that had started but were interrupted before their first model request now continue after a restart instead of being held back

When a conversation rewind is refused before it starts (the command queue is full or closed, the request fails, or the server rejects it), the rewind screen now shows why instead of returning to its choices with no message
A clean successor fork of a compacted session (its summary flattened ahead of the model's answer) is no longer counted as a mismatched seed: the answered summary is its context run, not a turn
When `muse attach --stdio` gives up on a session host that is slow to start, the start log its error names is kept instead of deleted
After resuming a session, a question the agent asked can no longer be answered twice, so the agent gets exactly one answer
After a crash, reopening a chat in the terminal no longer starts a reply on its own — queued follow-ups and restored results wait for your next message instead

In `muse serve`, a background compaction started at the soft context threshold is now applied instead of being thrown away, so served sessions usually compact in the background instead of waiting on a blocking compaction at the hard threshold
Background task results, scheduled check-ins and watcher events no longer stop waking an idle session after a workflow worker finishes
Reopening a chat no longer drops completed workflow turns after compaction
Resuming a session after an interrupted compaction no longer fails when the leftover compaction records are large

After you pause a workflow, later context compactions keep working instead of failing every time; if a paused workflow can't be kept in the saved context, Muse tells you it can still be resumed in this session but not after a restart
While `/goal` works on its own, a progress reminder now comes after about 30 model calls without reported progress, as designed, instead of about 15, because each call is counted once
Scrolling back through earlier output with the mouse wheel or trackpad works again while a session runs; clicking in the input no longer moves the cursor
When one Workflow worker's results can't be claimed, background updates for every other session, its parent included, still wake an idle session; only that worker's update waits

With a goal reminder active, when the only thing left is the result of a watcher the agent started on a long job, the turn now ends instead of the agent polling; the watcher's notice wakes the agent to finish

On a Mac with a locked Keychain, such as over a remote login, signing in now says to run `security unlock-keychain` and restart Muse Code, with the Keychain's own error code, instead of showing only an internal code
The desktop app now shows the saved history of a conversation that Muse Code 1.4.9 to 1.4.14 still has open in a terminal, instead of an empty history
In `muse serve`, a background compaction whose summary finishes while the next turn is running is now applied when that turn ends, instead of being discarded when that turn starts its own compaction

A host that `muse attach --stdio <id>` starts now lists that session from its first `session/list`, with the session that opened it (`spawnedBy`), even when the session's previous host exited before indexing it
Terminals that show program status (OSC 7501) now see Muse as waiting for you when a turn ends by asking a question in plain text, instead of done
Sandboxed commands and hooks no longer fail at random with "Can't find source path" while another sandboxed process in the same workspace exits

In a terminal pane only 5 or 6 rows tall, the end of a turn no longer leaves a blank-looking session: the last line of the conversation stays visible above the typing area, so a session with history no longer looks like a fresh start
Keep Goal recovery usable when compaction leaves a paused workflow behind

Over the session protocol, resuming a session the host still has loaded after its log was deleted or replaced outside Muse now refuses with a message that says so and how to go on, instead of answering that the session was not found or resuming it as if its log were intact

When /feedback or /bug cannot upload because there is no Model API key, the message now says how to get the report sent: set a Model API key so /feedback can send it, or, as a Meta employee, use the internal Muse build
Workflow workers no longer get a background-command reminder queued while their turn is still running, which could stop them from submitting their result
A hosted session no longer skips a compaction checkpoint after a subagent's write to the same session file recovers from a disk error
Code blocks inside quotes keep their indentation and highlighting, and their fence lines no longer show
Through `muse serve` and the SDKs, stopping a subagent that another subagent started now stops it instead of failing
Avoid a false active work warning when quitting a resumed fork

A periodic context save that fails, for example on a storage error, no longer ends the turn; the save is skipped with a note of why and the turn goes on, and a save whose cleanup of older history fails still counts as saved
After a crash, a `!` command that had not finished is marked cancelled with a note that it may have run, instead of an empty result

When queued background work cannot be started, the failure is now written to the local diagnostics that `/feedback` sends, and to the terminal outside the full-screen view, instead of being silently dropped

A chat keeps the name saved in its own history when you open it, even if Muse's separate list of names has lost it; before, it could get a new automatic name and `muse resume <name>` stopped finding it
Truncated shell output keeps its correct total size when output arrives slowly
Over the session protocol, resuming a session that a client had left with `session/leave` no longer reports that its last run ended abnormally
Sandboxed hooks and commands no longer fail at random with "Can't find source path" when another sandboxed process in the same session starts or exits
Stopping a paused workflow now still reports the stop after Muse restarts
On macOS, pasting a screenshot with Cmd+V now attaches it in terminals that send an empty paste for images, such as VS Code and Cursor

Right after an upgrade, `muse attach <session-name>` now waits for the session index to finish reading session names (it prints "indexing session names after an upgrade..." while it waits, as `muse resume <name>` does) instead of refusing that the session-name authority is unavailable; before, every retry refused the same way

Reading a forked or rewound conversation over the session protocol now shows the messages you sent in its copied turns that were missing before: each message of a turn that began with several, a message with an image, and a message you sent while the original turn was still working
Terminals that show program status (OSC 7501) now see Muse as waiting for you when a quick turn ends on a plain-text question before Muse confirms your message, instead of done

A long `muse exec` session that resumes for every prompt no longer stops saving its checkpoints after a few thousand prompts, because every session now drops the records of prompts that the conversation summary has already replaced
Clarify guidance to decode Workflow report fields before quoting them verbatim, keep literal escapes, and place commentary outside the quote
During the five seconds that a hook's block, failure or timeout notice shows in the lower-right corner, another hook's message no longer replaces it and is not shown
After Muse Code restarts from a crash, messages you queued before the crash now run before your next message, once each and in the order you sent them; before, your new message ran first

With a goal reminder active, a background command the agent stopped itself (or saw finish while checking on it) no longer counts as still running, so the reminder can send the agent back to unfinished work instead of leaving the session idle with nothing left to wake it
Apps connected to `muse serve --listen` now get the `session/started` notification before the reply to `session/start`, the same order as over stdio
A subagent whose definition declares memory no longer stops with a memory error partway through its work, and it now saves its context when its history is compacted, so reopening it stays fast
A paused workflow now stays resumable after Muse restarts even when a context compaction happens before any session checkpoint

When Muse asks a clarifying question, the recommended option now keeps the full scope you asked for instead of offering a reduced or skeleton variant, and on a request that already settles the outcome it proceeds without stopping to ask
Restore missing Workflow failure notifications when a child start cannot be confirmed
Rewind works in forked conversations, including copied messages and new messages added after the fork
After a crash during automatic naming, a chat whose history already holds its name keeps that name on the next start instead of getting a new automatic one

In `muse serve`, when a busy session has not started a message within 30 seconds, the message is now withdrawn with a busy error you can retry, instead of an internal error after which it could still run later
`muse exec` with a model already chosen no longer exits when the model catalog service answers with no models; it prints one notice and runs that model
A `muse exec` session that resumes for every prompt no longer adds a record per prompt to every saved checkpoint, which made such sessions stop saving checkpoints after a few thousand prompts
`/stop all` in a subagent's thread now stops that subagent's own running subagents instead of reporting the stop as failed
A `muse serve` chat that an older Muse version still holds open now shows its saved history when its log had an unreadable stretch, instead of showing no history

When you resume a session and its log is deleted or replaced outside Muse before Muse saves anything new to it, Muse now tells you what happened to it instead of quietly starting a new log or writing into the replacement. A session log or folder moved away outside Muse is no longer re-created empty, so moving it back keeps saving in the same place

When the model catalog lists no visible model, Muse now starts on the newest hidden model it grants you and names it in a startup notice, instead of stopping with "model catalog has no visible models"
After a crash, a question the agent was still waiting on can be answered even when earlier work in the session was compacted

After a model switch makes a chat unable to continue, Muse now says why and that starting a new session continues the work with this session's history kept, instead of only saying the turn could not prepare the conversation
A session started by a newer Muse no longer disappears from session lists while an older Muse process keeps running on the same machine

A session whose first prompt is very large, for example a log file of several megabytes, no longer drops out of the session list in apps that list your sessions, and you can still resume it and send more prompts; the session title shows the first 1,000 characters of that prompt
A prompt queued through the session protocol while a finished turn's follow-up waits to start now reports its own turn, so a client that waits on that turn gets its answer
Subscriber sessions no longer fail with "Model not found" when the model list arrives after sign-in
When a Workflow finishes after its script handled a failed agent call, Muse no longer tells the agent that the Workflow failed, so the agent no longer reports a finished Workflow as failed
When a long thread goes over the model's context window, the automatic smaller retry now drops enough older messages to fit instead of being refused again
After a session storage error clears, a Workflow agent that already finished no longer shows as scheduled or running again when the Workflow settles
Skill reminders no longer steer the agent onto a different skill when a skill it already loaded covers the same step
`muse mcp login` works after adding the first server to a fresh config
Fixed re-loading a chat's failed view while a tool streams output, which could fail with `projectionRebuildFailed`

Stopping a turn over the session protocol while a shell command's second permission ask is open, after you allowed the first one, no longer makes every later prompt in that session fail with "approval replay failed" or stay queued

`muse attach <session>` from a terminal to a session a `muse serve` host is running now says at once that a terminal can't join it yet and to keep using the window that runs it, instead of opening the resume picker and reporting the session as already in use

A chat whose automatic compaction keeps failing at the context limit no longer pays for a new summary on every request; after 2 failures in a row, Muse stops automatic compaction for that chat until a compaction works or you reopen it, and `/compact` still works

A session whose recent turns hold many full-size images, such as dozens of screenshots, can still be resumed after its context fills up; before, the compaction that followed could leave the session impossible to resume. If automatic compaction stops because those images make the compacted context too big to save, the stop notice now says so
Resuming a chat no longer repeats subagent completion messages or shows new child work as finished
When you report that a change does not show up in your own run, the agent is now prompted to trace the code path you ran instead of stopping at setup or flag steps
When a reminder such as a goal keeps a turn going after its answer and you press Esc while Muse is thinking again, the answer now shows Interrupted under it
A session no longer skips a compaction checkpoint when a Goal turn ended while its Workflow kept running and later finished
Forking a chat that contains an empty turn whose start was not recorded is now refused with a message saying why, instead of creating a fork that fails to open

In a compacted session, an image prompt that you send after you reopen the session now stays in the model's context after the next reopen, and `/compact` works again in that session; you cannot yet rewind to that turn or fork from it
IDE and other session-protocol clients now show the same warning as the terminal when a paused workflow is left out of a saved context checkpoint (`NoticeOrigin` gains `workflowCheckpoint`)
A prompt with an image is no longer dropped when the context is compacted at the start of its turn, so the agent answers that prompt instead of the previous one
A fork whose seed would fail to load elsewhere is now refused at creation with a clear error instead of publishing and then failing to open
Fixed a race where re-loading a chat's failed view during a running turn could fail with `projectionRebuildFailed`

A `session/resume` check (`admitOnly: true`) no longer makes the checking client a driver of the session, sends `session/driveChanged` (experimental) to its other clients, or re-sends it the session's pending approval and user-input requests; a `session/resume` without `admitOnly` still joins the session's drivers, as before
In `muse serve`, leaving a chat that another connected client is driving no longer stops and unloads it under that client: `session/leave` answers `sessionInUse` and the chat stays loaded

Aborting `Session.run` in the TypeScript and Python SDKs while its turn is still queued and the host is busy now keeps taking the turn back, so the turn no longer runs after the abort; in Python, cancelling again returns at once while the take-back still finishes
A Workflow resume that stops because an agent's saved start record is damaged now reports the plain reason and next step in its result and in the Latest error row, not only an error code

The "session log flush degraded" note at the end of a turn no longer goes missing when a queued message or a model, approval or reasoning-effort change was refused once because a save had failed earlier in the turn
The first message you send after an automatic compaction finishes in the background now builds on its summary, instead of requesting another summary and dropping the recent turn that summary kept
Through `muse serve` and the SDKs, a subagent that was interrupted and resumed no longer shows its earlier run's late result as its own while the new run is working
Branching a forked or side session right after it compacts, before its next message, no longer fails with a fork seed count mismatch

A session running Workflows no longer gets stuck unable to save its context when a Workflow capacity record has lost its launch record; that one Workflow can no longer resume its children after a restart, and the session keeps saving and continuing
Preserve subagent Stop information when reopening a chat
